speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I had touched on this briefly in July last year, but I think it is worth restating some of these points.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since Pakatan Harapan's victory in the Malaysian general election in May 2018, Singapore has consistently expressed our hope for good and mutually beneficial relations with the new Malaysian government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We want to continue working closely with Malaysia, at both the federal and the state levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do so on the basis of equality and mutual respect.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this means working through any differences and outstanding issues amicably, constructively and in accordance with international law and international norms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We believe that both countries need to deepen our strategic trust and develop new areas of cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We agreed in the spirit of good neighbourliness and hoped that this would set the tone for a positive and fruitful relationship with Malaysia’s new government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since then, we have maintained this cooperative approach with several high-level bilateral visits and exchanges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee hosted Prime Minister Mahathir for an official visit to Singapore in November last year, in conjunction with the 33rd ASEAN Summit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During the meeting between the two Prime Ministers, they acknowledged that there would always be elements of both competition and cooperation, but both of them saw a bright future for Malaysia and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In any close relationship with complex historical legacies, problems will arise from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is to be expected between such close neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The only question is how we approach these problems.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both of these sets of sudden actions upset the status quo that has been in place for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These actions did not bode well for our bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There has been strong public interest in these matters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, today, I would like to set out the facts of each issue and highlight the steps that both countries have taken to find a constructive way forward.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members of the House, may I refer you to this map which is displayed, which reflects Malaysia's unilateral extension to the hatched area.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The waters in this area are tight, less than 24 nautical miles wide.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This purported extension goes beyond even Malaysia’s own territorial sea claims according to Malaysia's own 1979 map, which Singapore has consistently rejected.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The inescapable conclusion is that the new Johor Bahru Port Limits transgress into what are indisputably Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore has long exercised sovereignty and patrolled these waters without any protest from Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: However, since late November 2018, Malaysian government vessels started intruding into these Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have protested the purported extension and these intrusions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have also increased our security presence in the area in order to safeguard our waters and sovereignty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am sure Members of this House would join me in commending our security agencies which have been acting professionally, responsibly, and with restraint, in order to minimise the risks of untoward incidents at sea.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our extension was done in accordance with international law and remained well within Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On 10 December 2018, the Malaysian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a press statement committing to "take all effective measures to de-escalate the situation on the ground".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Despite this statement, daily intrusions by Malaysian government vessels into our territorial waters have continued.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These intrusions do not help Malaysia's legal case.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: All they do is to raise tensions and endanger navigational safety in the area.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is a need to calm the situation at sea.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It was in this context that I met Minister Saifuddin on 8 January 2019.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members would have read the Joint Press Statement that we issued after our meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore believes that maritime boundary delimitation is best resolved through negotiations, to reach an amicable settlement acceptable to all parties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If negotiations are unsuccessful, Singapore is prepared to settle such disputes by recourse to an appropriate international dispute settlement procedure.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This declaration means that other States Parties to UNCLOS cannot unilaterally commence third-party arbitration or adjudication against Singapore in respect of maritime boundary disputes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore likewise cannot unilaterally commence third-party arbitration or adjudication against other UNCLOS States Parties for such disputes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has to be by mutual agreement: both sides have to agree to the terms of third-party arbitration or adjudication in the event that bilateral negotiations are unsuccessful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore remains committed to finding an amicable resolution through dialogue with our Malaysian partners and this is what the working group led by the two Foreign Ministries will try to achieve.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On airspace, there have actually been two developments.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, the new Instrument Landing System (ILS) for Seletar Airport.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Put simply, an ILS is an aid for pilots to land safely at an airport during bad weather or when there is low visibility conditions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Seletar Airport actually meets all the relevant requirements of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) on airport design and operations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Planes have been safely flying in and out of Seletar Airport for decades, using the same flight routes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we did not previously have an ILS.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We now installed the ILS at Seletar Airport at the request of Firefly, a subsidiary of Malaysian Airlines.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Firefly had agreed to move its operations to Seletar Airport by 1 December 2018.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But Firefly informed the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) that the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) required all Malaysian carriers to only operate to airports with an instrument approach.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ironically, CAAS was actually trying to facilitate Firefly’s operations at Seletar by installing the ILS, the same ILS which Malaysia has now objected to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: CAAS sought early consultation with CAAM on the implementation of the ILS procedures at Seletar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: CAAS formally approached the Malaysian agency in December 2017 but received no response for almost a year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: CAAM only replied in November 2018, objecting for the first time to the proposed ILS procedures, and citing alleged consequences on the future development of Pasir Gudang.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Despite this delay, CAAS addressed all their concerns.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is important to note that the ILS uses exactly the same flight paths that aircraft landing at Seletar have used all along for visual flights.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Flight procedures, such as those for the Seletar ILS, are a basic element of civil aviation, which inform pilots on what they need to do in order to land or take off safely.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There have been claims that the ILS flight path will more strictly restrict the height of buildings below it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There were allegations that Pasir Gudang will not be able to have buildings higher than five stories because of the ILS.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But if Members drive across the Causeway and drive around Pasir Gudang, you will see that there are, in fact, already structures that are as tall as 105 metres, and this, by the way, is taller than many Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we have consistently stated that if Malaysia has any new plans for new developments, we are prepared to discuss and to adjust the ILS procedures, if necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ultimately, the purpose of the ILS procedures is to improve safety and facilitate flights and, in this case, especially for Malaysia’s own Firefly, which services many smaller Malaysian airports.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: CAAS met CAAM on 29 November 2018 to address their concerns.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Following this meeting, CAAS published the ILS procedures for Seletar Airport on 1 December 2018.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This was done in accordance with Singapore's responsibilities under the relevant ICAO requirements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, it published the ILS procedures in accordance with our responsibilities under the relevant ICAO requirements as well as the bilateral arrangements between Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And to give the aviation community time to prepare for the ILS, it set the effective date for the implementation of ILS as 3 January 2019, a timeline which is entirely in line with international norms.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: During this period, on 12 December 2018, CAAM issued a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM).

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And this NOTAM unilaterally declared the airspace over Pasir Gudang as an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) operation area from 13 to 28 December 2018.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This Restricted Area would force flights operating to and from Seletar Airport to spiral up and down close to the airport in order to traverse above the Restricted Area at 6,000 feet.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: All over the world, and this is a point worth emphasising, aviation is, by nature, transboundary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: CAAS, as the air traffic services provider for the area, was neither informed nor consulted even though these actions affected current civil aviation operations out of Seletar Airport.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It cut through an established international aviation route, and it affected flight efficiency and safety.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Malaysia’s declaration of a permanent Restricted Area escalated what was initially a matter concerning ILS procedures, which is a norm for many airports around the world, into a much more serious issue affecting all flights operating at Seletar Airport from the north.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This was not helpful for commercial aviation in the area and, furthermore, damaged the overall tenor of our bilateral relationship.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Unfortunately, Malaysia’s Firefly will still be unable to start operating at Seletar due to its own Malaysian regulator’s requirement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also agreed that the Transport Ministers from both countries should meet soon for discussions on these measures and to resolve the issues.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Transport Ministers, I believe, have agreed to meet later this month.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: After all, this has brought great economic benefits and tourism to both countries and, indeed, to our region.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As such, I look forward to the resolution of these issues in an amicable fashion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are other issues that we have to deal with.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore will do our best to discuss all outstanding bilateral issues with Malaysia in a calm, reasonable and focused manner.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This approach extends to other issues beyond the Johor Bahru Port Limits and the Seletar ILS procedures.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For example, Malaysia had earlier expressed their intention to review the 1974 Operational Letter of Agreement on airspace arrangements in southern Johor, and we had responded that we would review their proposal when we received it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Such discussions on air navigation arrangements involve consultations with international stakeholders and cannot be done overnight.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the meantime, in the interest of civil aviation safety, air traffic operations must continue according to the current arrangements and in accordance with ICAO requirements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Prime Minister Mahathir raised this with Prime Minister Lee when they met last November.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Unfortunately, their discussions were overshadowed by the new issues that had arisen over the Johor Bahru Port Limits and the Seletar ILS procedures.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the two Attorneys-General will meet again to continue their discussions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As an example, Singapore was scheduled to host a meeting on the Joint Ministerial Committee (JMC) for Iskandar Malaysia this morning.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The meeting was to be chaired by Minister Lawrence Wong and Malaysian Economic Affairs Minister Azmin Ali.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This intrusion by the Johor Menteri Besar went against the spirit of the agreement between Foreign Minister Saifuddin and me just the day before.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I also informed both Minister Saifuddin and Minister Azmin of this postponement, and I should add that my discussions with both Ministers, both before and after the Johor Menteri Besar’s actions, have been amicable and constructive, and we have focused on trying to resolve issues and not to wind things up.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This morning, he also met Minister Khaw Boon Wan and Minister Lawrence Wong to discuss several bilateral projects which he is in charge of.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But both sides must act in good faith, in compliance with international law and norms, and honour existing agreements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The strength of Singapore’s diplomacy depends on domestic unity and resilience, and the fact that we cannot be intimidated or bought.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is the foundation for our diplomacy even as we seek good relations with all our friends and neighbours within a rules-based international order.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is why Total Defence and our investment in the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) are so important.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Resilience includes improving our water supply infrastructure, namely, NEWater and desalinated water, strengthening our food security by diversifying our food sources, and ensuring that we have a strong, diversified labour market.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As a small state with limited resources, the quest for security and resilience has been a constant, relentless imperative for us since Independence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not something that we look at only in times of unease.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am confident that we can continue to rely on strong bipartisan support from this House, and the unity of purpose among all Singaporeans, as we strive to ensure that Singapore’s independence, territorial sovereignty, safety, security and prosperity are secured for this generation and those to come.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The flight path for Seletar airbase is the same, whether with ILS or without ILS.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But from what we heard from the Malaysia Transport Minister Anthony Loke, he kept saying that it will prevent the development of Pasir Gudang, especially the tall buildings.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask whether the Minister, Anthony Loke, has different calculation or miscalculated, or is he, as how my residents put it, I quote, "frying roti prata"?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, my favourite Minister for Transport, Mr Khaw Boon Wan, who is meeting with him, will seek a clarification on this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to engage in speculation as to the basis for his calculations and assumptions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think it is best that both sides meet, set out their respective concerns and find a constructive way forward.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Ultimately, we have to look at these emotive issues through cold, calculative lenses by taking deliberate steps to advance Singapore's interests, and our resolve to take such steps should not be underestimated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My question for the Minister is: what positive actions and active steps can Singaporeans do to protect and preserve our sovereign rights?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point is that we do need more bilateral consultations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As for Singaporeans, I mentioned just now that foreign policy begins at home, the unity of purpose, the calm way in which Singaporeans have responded to this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But actually, both countries, and I think especially the businessmen on both sides, are aware of how our economies are intertwined, and these sorts of disputes are unnecessary and unhelpful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, calmly, resolutely, firmly asserting our sovereignty and our rights, and then quietly taking appropriate actions is probably the wisest course at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to speculate as to other measures which we would have to consider at appropriate times.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: From the bilateral talks and discussions, both official and non-official, does the Minister sense that the Malaysian government is sincere in resolving the various bilateral issues between the two countries on a win-win basis?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is a salient question, but actually, more complicated than it sounds.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First of all, we start on the basis that we are two sovereign nations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we are two sovereign nations with a complicated history and, therefore, we must always expect problems to arise.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They will arise and, as I said just now, the only question is how we approach these problems and, as to the point behind the Member's question, the spirit behind our attempts to resolve this problem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When dealing with foreign policy, I find it very useful to clearly separate in my mind national interest from personal ties and personal relationships.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the case of Singapore, our top, paramount imperative is to protect our sovereignty and independence, and our national interests.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our second imperative is to abide by international law.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our third imperative is to fully honour all agreements which we have solemnly entered into.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because, after all, if you do not honour past agreements, what value do future agreements have?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is only after you settle these three things – national interests, international law, and abiding by agreements – then the individuals, the Ministers, the officials and the agencies come into it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We both concluded that it is important that Ministers and officials keep the attitude of trying to solve problems, not aggravate them, not make them worse.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope they also reflect a larger body of opinion within Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Understand that the long-term interest of Singapore and Malaysia is best secured by working together, resolving differences, expanding areas of collaboration, and looking for new things that we can do.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: One point which I also discussed with Minister Azmin who is, as Members know, in charge of economic affairs, I said, look, the world is changing at such a rapid manner.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We need to focus on updating, upscaling, transforming our economies and working together, and not be caught using unnecessary bandwidth fighting unnecessary conflicts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So sorry to give the Member a long answer.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we always aim for good interpersonal ties, we always talk about friendship between countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But remember that friendship between countries is to advance national interest.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You never compromise national interest in order to have better relations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, it is a discipline which I always maintain in all my relations with my counterparts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am pretty sure if you spoke to Minister Saifuddin or Minister Azmin, they would say something pretty much the same.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I do my best to make sure I am never the cause, the source of a problem.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Shortly after that, the Johor Mentri Besar came in.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, it may well be that the Minister's counterparts are sincere, but does that reflect the entire Malaysian government?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: If they are not able to properly control or represent the rest of the Malaysian government, what can Singapore do in the event we get further intrusions into our waters or airspace?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Obviously, one option is bilateral discussions, which we are doing.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But if one side is being sincere, and the other side is not, or is not able to follow through with actions, what can we do?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I would be grateful for the Minister's thoughts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In popular parlance, it is called "good cop, bad cop".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do not play those sorts of things.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I cannot speak for Malaysia, but I can speak for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I always say the same thing to all my counterparts that Singapore does not have the luxury of saying different things to different people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In any case, we believe it is this reputation for consistency and constancy that adds to our reputation of reliability and integrity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Sometimes, it may come across as we are boringly consistent, and we seem to studiously avoid chest-thumping and other manifestations of nationalism.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I would submit that this is the appropriate posture for a small, tiny nation-state like Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Not that we are passive, not that we give in, but consistency.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Now, specifically, dealing with a counterpart or another country which may not obey the same conventions and rules.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Could we just let it pass in the name of, well, we just had a successful meeting, we are getting along, let us not sour that?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I hope Members appreciate this fine line that I am trying to follow, to be resolute, but to be calm, to quietly but clearly protect our interests.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It does not mean we do not have sharp elbows.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And sometimes, if we have to do it, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But again, as I said, it is still early days, so let us see how this evolves.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other point I would make, especially for younger Singaporeans, is that the nature of the relationship between Malaysia and Singapore will always be unique and special.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we must never be surprised, both at the upside and the downside.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is, in psychological parlance, what you would call an “emotionally labile” relationship.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must not be caught surprised or flat-footed about it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I believe we should not aggravate the emotional angst but, at the same time, we must also firmly protect our interests and to tell the other side that there will be consequences for actions that are taken against Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Many Singapore companies employ Malaysians, and they are essential for us doing business.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Singaporeans also love to go to Malaysia for sightseeing and to shop and dine.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Last month, Minister Shanmugam said that Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers had worked their guts out to clear the crowds at the Causeway so that Singaporeans can pass through the checkpoint better.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, in the midst of these sea and air disputes, what is the message that we want to send to Singaporeans to help to manage this relationship better?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Maybe that is something the Member should express rather than me.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And Malaysia has certainly provided Singaporeans with a valuable national education lesson.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because provocation after provocation, so far, what we seem to be doing is, every time something happens, we say, "Don't do it again." We are firm about it, but then it happens again, and we say, "Don't do it again." Dozens of red lines may have been crossed.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To use the same popular parlance that the Minister had used earlier, will there be a point in time that this good cop has to be a bit of a bad cop, for our northern neighbours to understand clearer and beyond doubt that any further provocation will be met with an equal reaction on our part?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is another very good question, which requires an answer.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I hope that Members also appreciate that as the Foreign Minister, by definition, there are some things which I cannot say and I should not say.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I want to clear up this confusion that they are the ones who have the licence to provoke and that we respond, but without an equal and opposite response.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We need to maintain unity of purpose, consensus and a collective spirit to stand united.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because what if that domestic consensus is eroded or broken?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My words will carry no weight in any international negotiations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second, maybe the Member should ask Minister Ng Eng Hen tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I have already said and I only have one sentence on the SAF.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But to say Total Defence and our investment over decades in the SAF make a big difference; it makes a big difference.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are some incidents which I cannot relate today.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But simply knowing that we have a credible and strong SAF again makes diplomacy much easier.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Third, in the spirit of candidness, sincerity and openness, we are trying to resolve these issues, because, in fact, for the specific issues that have been raised, I can see a way forward to resolve all of them.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And so long as there is a possibility, a probability of resolving it, then our current tack of making sure the situation remains calm and that we do not allow the situation to escalate out of hand into what I described just now as a downward spiral of measures and countermeasures, it is still the appropriate thing to do.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Fourth, I also said that despite our attempts to be constructive and to keep the avenue open for a negotiated settlement, our neighbours must not believe that they can take actions without impact, without consequences on themselves.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am not going to enumerate them now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But this concept that for every action you take there are consequences, we will do so quietly but effectively.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Red lines are not something you draw lightly and not something which you should pronounce publicly without having carefully thought through all the consequences and without communicating those considerations clearly and unambiguously to the person you are negotiating with on the other side.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I hope Members of this House and Singaporeans will understand that some of these are best conducted behind-the-scenes, quietly, and that is why I do not believe in megaphone diplomacy.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I want to ask the Minister whether the Johor authorities appreciate what Singapore had done and, if not, should we look at reviewing the terms again on how we supply treated water to Johor?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Minister Heng Swee Keat has reminded me to tell Members that this additional assistance is over and above the agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the Member has brought up an important issue, water, and the Water Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have stated our position several times in this House.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is because this agreement was guaranteed by both governments.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the case of Malaysia, at the federal level, and in our case, the Singapore level, at the point of Independence.
